experiences.name: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park
experiences.description: Experience hanami (flower viewing) under the iconic weeping cherry tree in Kyoto's most famous park. Join locals for picnics beneath thousands of blooming sakura trees, with food stalls offering traditional snacks like sakura mochi and taiyaki. The park is especially magical at night when lanterns illuminate the blossoms.

experiences.name: Senso-ji Temple & Nakamise Shopping Street
experiences.description: Visit Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple, founded in 628 AD. Walk through the Thunder Gate (Kaminarimon) and explore the vibrant Nakamise shopping street lined with traditional craft shops and street food vendors. Families can try fortune-telling omikuji slips and dress in rented kimono for memorable photos.

experiences.name: Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum & Park
experiences.description: A deeply moving and historically essential experience for families. Tour the Peace Memorial Museum to understand the events of 1945 through personal artifacts and testimonies, then walk through the Peace Memorial Park to see the Atomic Bomb Dome. Children can fold origami cranes at the Children's Peace Monument, connecting with Sadako's powerful story.
experiences.location: Peace Memorial Park, Naka Ward, Hiroshima

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into Japan's legendary food culture with a self-guided or guided tour of the Tsukiji Outer Market. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), grilled scallops, matcha ice cream, and wagyu beef skewers. This is an ideal family activity that introduces everyone to authentic Japanese flavors in a lively, accessible market setting.
experiences.location: Tsukiji Outer Market, Chuo City, Tokyo

experiences.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove & Togetsukyo Bridge
experiences.description: Wander through the ethereal bamboo forest of Arashiyama, one of Japan's most iconic natural and cultural landscapes. Extend the experience with a rickshaw ride through the historic district, visit the Tenryu-ji Zen garden (a UNESCO World Heritage Site), and stroll across the Togetsukyo Bridge with stunning mountain and cherry blossom backdrops in spring. Perfect for all ages.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Japan
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at airport around 22:30. Clear customs and immigration, then take the airport limousine bus or train to your accommodation (Aegean Bliss Resort). Most budget-friendly option is the train/subway combination. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest to prepare for the trip ahead.

meals.breakfast: N/A - In flight
meals.lunch: N/A - In flight
meals.dinner: Grab a quick and affordable bite at the airport convenience store (7-Eleven or Lawson) or airport food court. Onigiri (rice balls), instant ramen, or a bento box will cost around ¥500–¥1,000.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a Suica or Pasmo IC card at the airport for easy train/bus travel throughout Japan. Also consider picking up a pocket Wi-Fi or SIM card at the airport for navigation. Keep receipts for tax-free shopping eligibility.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a slow morning to recover from jet lag. After breakfast, head to the nearby area around your hotel to explore local streets, a morning market, or a nearby shrine. Visit a local neighborhood shrine for a peaceful cultural introduction. Many are free to enter and offer a quiet, authentic Japanese experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Senso-ji Temple & Nakamise Shopping Street in Asakusa — Tokyo's oldest Buddhist temple founded in 628 AD. Walk through the iconic Kaminarimon (Thunder Gate), stroll the Nakamise shopping arcade for affordable souvenirs like keychains, fans, and snacks (¥100–¥500 per item), and explore the temple grounds. Entry to the temple is free.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Sumida River area near Senso-ji for a relaxed evening stroll. The area often has beautiful cherry blossom views along the riverbanks in April. Enjoy the illuminated Skytree views from the riverside for free. Return to the hotel by 9 PM.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast at 7-Eleven or FamilyMart near the hotel — onigiri, tamagoyaki (egg roll), and canned coffee for around ¥400–¥600.
meals.lunch: Eat at a ramen shop near Asakusa. A hearty bowl of ramen costs ¥700–¥1,000. Look for standing ramen bars for the most budget-friendly option.
meals.dinner: Enjoy a budget dinner at a local izakaya (Japanese pub) near Asakusa. Order yakitori skewers, edamame, and a small beer for ¥1,500–¥2,500 per person. Look for set menus (teishoku) for the best value.

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is busiest on weekends. Arrive early (before 9 AM) to avoid crowds. The Nakamise shops open around 10 AM. Wear comfortable walking shoes — you'll be on your feet most of the day. Budget tip: Many temples and shrines in Japan are free to enter.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Shinkansen (bullet train) or overnight bus from Tokyo toward Kyoto (book in advance for best prices; Shinkansen is about ¥13,000–¥14,000 one way, or use a JR Pass if purchased). Alternatively, take the highway bus for around ¥3,000–¥5,000 for a budget option. Arrive in Kyoto by midday. Check in or drop bags at a coin locker at Kyoto Station.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head directly to Maruyama Park for Cherry Blossom Viewing (Hanami). Experience the iconic weeping cherry tree — one of the most photographed in all of Japan. Spread a picnic blanket, enjoy the blossoms, and soak in the festive hanami atmosphere with locals and families. The park is free to enter. Explore nearby Yasaka Shrine, also free.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the Gion district — Kyoto's famous geisha quarter. Walk along Hanamikoji Street in the early evening for a chance to spot geiko or maiko. Browse traditional shops and enjoy the lantern-lit atmosphere. Visit a budget-friendly noodle or tofu restaurant in the area.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at Tokyo Station before boarding — a station bento (ekiben) is a quintessential Japanese travel experience for ¥800–¥1,200.
meals.lunch: Picnic in Maruyama Park! Stop at a konbini or local market near the park to pick up onigiri, sandwiches, and drinks for ¥600–¥900 per person.
meals.dinner: Try Kyoto-style cuisine at a budget ramen or soba restaurant near Gion. Look for restaurants with plastic food displays in the window — a sign of affordable, no-frills dining. Budget: ¥800–¥1,500 per person.

day_by_day.notes: April is peak cherry blossom season — Maruyama Park will be extremely crowded on weekends. Arrive in the afternoon for a more relaxed experience or in the evening when the trees are beautifully illuminated. Bring a tarp or blanket for hanami. Book Kyoto accommodations well in advance during cherry blossom season.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Fushimi Inari Taisha — the famous shrine with thousands of vermillion torii gates winding up a mountain. Entry is completely free. Start early (before 8 AM) to beat the crowds. Hike as far as you like — the full trail takes 2–3 hours round trip, but even the first 30 minutes offers stunning photo opportunities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel to Arashiyama district. Visit the Bamboo Grove (free to walk through), Tenryu-ji Temple gardens (¥500 entry for the garden), and stroll along the Oi River. Rent a bicycle near Arashiyama Station for easy exploration (around ¥1,000/day). Visit Monkey Park Iwatayama if the family enjoys wildlife (¥550 entry).
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Kyoto. Visit Nishiki Market — Kyoto's famous 'Kitchen Street' — for affordable street food tastings. Try pickled vegetables, tamagoyaki, fresh mochi, and grilled skewers for ¥100–¥400 per item. A great family-friendly evening food adventure.

meals.breakfast: Early convenience store breakfast before heading to Fushimi Inari. Budget: ¥400–¥600.
meals.lunch: Grab lunch near Arashiyama — look for tofu cuisine restaurants or a simple udon shop. Budget: ¥700–¥1,200 per person.
meals.dinner: Graze through Nishiki Market for a fun, affordable dinner of street food snacks. Budget: ¥1,000–¥1,500 per person for a satisfying variety of bites.

day_by_day.notes: Fushimi Inari is one of Japan's most visited sites — go as early as possible. The Arashiyama Bamboo Grove is also very crowded; aim for early morning or late afternoon. Nishiki Market closes around 6 PM, so plan your timing accordingly. Most vendors are cash-only.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion) — one of Japan's most iconic landmarks. Entry is ¥500 per adult. The temple is surrounded by beautiful gardens and a reflective pond. Arrive early to beat tour groups. Afterward, walk or take a short bus ride to Ryoan-ji Temple, famous for its enigmatic Zen rock garden (entry ¥600).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Nijo Castle — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a fascinating piece of samurai-era history. The 'nightingale floors' squeak as you walk, a historical security feature. Entry is ¥1,030 for adults. Explore the beautiful Ninomaru Palace and surrounding gardens. Great for families interested in history.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed evening near Kyoto Station. Browse the Kyoto Station building itself — a modern architectural marvel with free observation decks and affordable restaurants on the 11th floor (Kyoto Ramen Koji is a must-visit for budget ramen lovers). Prepare for tomorrow's travel to Hiroshima.

meals.breakfast: Morning set meal at a local kissaten (traditional Japanese coffee shop) near your accommodation. Expect toast, egg, and coffee for ¥500–¥800.
meals.lunch: Eat at a nearby shokudo (casual Japanese diner) near Kinkaku-ji or Ryoan-ji. A teishoku set meal (rice, miso soup, main dish) costs ¥800–¥1,200.
meals.dinner: Kyoto Ramen Koji on the 10th floor of Kyoto Station — multiple famous ramen shops in one location. Budget: ¥900–¥1,200 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a Kyoto City Bus Day Pass (¥700) for unlimited bus rides — it covers Kinkaku-ji, Ryoan-ji, and Nijo Castle efficiently. Book Hiroshima accommodation and Shinkansen tickets today if not already done.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early Shinkansen from Kyoto to Hiroshima (approximately 1 hour, ¥5,720 or covered by JR Pass). Check bags into a coin locker at Hiroshima Station. Head immediately to the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum & Park. Allow at least 2–3 hours for the museum — it is a deeply moving, historically essential experience. Entry is ¥200 per adult (one of Japan's most affordable major museums).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Peace Memorial Park. Visit the A-Bomb Dome (Genbaku Dome) — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and haunting reminder of the 1945 atomic bombing. Walk through the park, visit the Children's Peace Monument and the Flame of Peace. The park is free to explore. Afterward, take a tram to Hiroshima Castle (¥370 entry) for a samurai history experience with great city views from the top.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Hiroshima's famous local dish — okonomiyaki (savory pancake). Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki is layered differently from Osaka-style and is a must-try. Head to Okonomimura (Okonomiyaki Village) — a multi-story building with dozens of small okonomiyaki stalls. A full meal costs ¥900–¥1,300.

meals.breakfast: Grab an early breakfast at Kyoto Station before boarding the Shinkansen. Convenience store or station bakery. Budget: ¥400–¥700.
meals.lunch: Simple lunch near Peace Memorial Park — many affordable cafes and bento shops in the area. Budget: ¥700–¥1,000.
meals.dinner: Okonomimura for Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki. A filling, authentic, and budget-friendly dinner. Budget: ¥900–¥1,300 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Peace Memorial Museum is emotionally intense — prepare children with age-appropriate context beforehand. The museum has English audio guides and exhibits. Hiroshima trams (streetcars) are an affordable and convenient way to get around the city (¥180–¥220 per ride or ¥700 for a day pass).

day_by_day.morning: Take a short ferry from Hiroshima to Miyajima Island (ferry is ¥180 each way from Miyajimaguchi pier; JR Pass holders ride free on the JR Ferry). Visit the iconic Itsukushima Shrine with its famous floating torii gate — especially magical at high tide. Entry to the shrine is ¥300. Explore the island's free walking paths and beautiful coastal scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike up Mount Misen on Miyajima for panoramic views of the Seto Inland Sea (free to hike; ropeway option available for ¥1,000 one way). Encounter the friendly wild deer that roam freely around the island — a big hit with families. Explore Daisho-in Temple at the base of the mountain (free entry) — a fascinating complex with hundreds of small statues.
day_by_day.evening: Return by ferry to Hiroshima. Enjoy a relaxed evening in Hiroshima's Hondori shopping arcade — a covered pedestrian street great for window shopping and affordable eats. Try local street food like momiji manju (maple leaf-shaped cakes filled with red bean paste, ¥100–¥150 each).

meals.breakfast: Early convenience store breakfast before catching the ferry. Budget: ¥400–¥600.
meals.lunch: Eat lunch on Miyajima Island. Try grilled oysters (Hiroshima oysters are famous) at a beachside stall for ¥300–¥500 per oyster, or grab a budget set meal at a local restaurant for ¥900–¥1,300.
meals.dinner: Casual dinner in Hiroshima's city center. Try a budget Chinese restaurant (Hiroshima has a strong Chinese food culture) or a gyudon (beef bowl) chain like Yoshinoya or Sukiya for ¥400–¥700.

day_by_day.notes: Check the tide schedule for Miyajima before visiting — the floating torii gate is most impressive at high tide. The island can get very crowded midday; aim to arrive early. Deer on the island are wild and may grab food from bags — keep snacks secured!

day_by_day.morning: Take the Shinkansen back toward Osaka (approximately 1.5 hours from Hiroshima, ¥9,440 or JR Pass). Arrive in Osaka and check in or drop bags. Head to Osaka Castle — one of Japan's most famous landmarks. Explore the castle tower (¥600 entry) and the expansive surrounding park, which is also a popular cherry blossom spot in April.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Dotonbori district — Osaka's vibrant entertainment and food hub. Walk along the Dotonbori canal, see the famous Glico Running Man sign, and browse the lively street food scene. Visit Kuromon Ichiba Market (Osaka's Kitchen) for fresh food stalls and local produce. Entry to the market area is free.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Osaka's legendary street food scene in Dotonbori for dinner. Osaka is known as the 'Nation's Kitchen' — try takoyaki (octopus balls, ¥500–¥700 for 8 pieces), kushikatsu (deep-fried skewers, ¥100–¥200 per skewer), and taiyaki (fish-shaped cakes). A full street food dinner can be had for ¥1,000–¥1,500.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at Hiroshima Station before departing — station bento or convenience store. Budget: ¥500–¥800.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Kuromon Market — sample fresh sashimi, tamagoyaki, and seasonal items for around ¥800–¥1,200.
meals.dinner: Street food feast in Dotonbori. Budget: ¥1,000–¥1,500 per person for a satisfying variety of Osaka specialties.

day_by_day.notes: Osaka is generally more affordable than Tokyo and Kyoto for food. The Osaka Amazing Pass (¥2,500/day) offers unlimited subway rides and free entry to many attractions — worth considering if you plan to use public transport frequently. Dotonbori is very lively in the evenings — great for families.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Shitennoji Temple — Japan's oldest officially administered temple, founded in 593 AD. Entry to the inner garden is ¥300; the outer grounds are free. A peaceful and historically significant site away from the tourist crowds. Afterward, explore the surrounding Tennoji area, including Tennoji Park and Zoo (zoo entry ¥500 — great for families).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Shinsekai — a retro, working-class neighborhood with a nostalgic 1950s atmosphere. Visit the Tsutenkaku Tower for panoramic city views (¥900 entry). Browse the quirky shops and try more kushikatsu at one of the many local restaurants. Explore the Namba area and Amerikamura (American Village) for free people-watching and street culture.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Osaka — enjoy a sit-down dinner at an affordable okonomiyaki restaurant (Osaka-style this time, mixed rather than layered). Visit a Don Quijote discount store for last-minute souvenir shopping — great prices on Japanese snacks, cosmetics, and novelty items. Stroll along the Dotonbori canal one last time for evening photos.

meals.breakfast: Morning set at a local Osaka kissaten or convenience store near your accommodation. Budget: ¥400–¥700.
meals.lunch: Kushikatsu lunch in Shinsekai — order at the counter, dip once in sauce (house rule!), and enjoy. Budget: ¥1,000–¥1,500 per person.
meals.dinner: Osaka-style okonomiyaki restaurant — many offer all-you-can-eat (tabehodai) options for around ¥1,500–¥2,000 per person. Great value for families.

day_by_day.notes: Shinsekai is a fascinating slice of old Osaka — safe to visit but has a gritty, authentic feel very different from tourist areas. The Tsutenkaku Tower is smaller than Tokyo Skytree but offers a charming, retro experience. Don Quijote stores are open until midnight or 24 hours — perfect for late-night souvenir runs.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Japan. If time allows before checkout, visit a nearby neighborhood park for one last cherry blossom viewing moment. Pack souvenirs carefully — Japan has strict customs rules about certain food items. Check out of accommodation and store bags at the station if your flight is in the afternoon or evening.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the airport (Kansai International Airport from Osaka, or Narita/Haneda if returning to Tokyo). Allow at least 2–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security. Browse duty-free shops for last-minute gifts — Japanese whisky, Kit Kat flavors, and matcha products make excellent souvenirs. Use remaining yen on airport food or snacks to bring home.
day_by_day.evening: Board your return flight. Reflect on an incredible 10 days exploring Japan's history, culture, cherry blossoms, and family-friendly attractions on a budget!

meals.breakfast: Final Japanese convenience store breakfast or a sit-down morning set at a local cafe. Savor that last cup of Japanese drip coffee! Budget: ¥500–¥900.
meals.lunch: Airport food court or terminal restaurant. Japanese airport food is high quality — try a final bowl of udon or soba for ¥800–¥1,200.
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport snacks depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary reminder: Key money-saving tips used throughout this trip — JR Pass for Shinkansen travel, IC card (Suica/Pasmo) for local transit, convenience store meals for breakfast, free shrine and temple grounds, free parks for hanami, and street food for affordable dinners. Total estimated daily budget per person (excluding transport): ¥5,000–¥8,000/day (approximately $33–$53 USD). A 10-day JR Pass (¥50,000) is highly recommended if purchased before arriving in Japan.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Tokyo/Osaka airport at 22:30 on UA flight. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange airport transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get settled. Grab a light snack from a convenience store (7-Eleven or FamilyMart) near the hotel if hungry.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or in transit
meals.dinner: Convenience store onigiri, sandwiches, or instant ramen from 7-Eleven or FamilyMart near the hotel – a classic and affordable Japanese late-night option (¥500–¥1,000)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is purely an arrival day. No activities are scheduled before landing. Purchase a Suica or IC card at the airport for seamless public transit use throughout the trip. Consider buying a pocket Wi-Fi or SIM card at the airport arrivals hall. Rest well – big days ahead!

day_by_day.morning: Start the trip with a visit to Senso-ji Temple & Nakamise Shopping Street in Asakusa – Tokyo's oldest Buddhist temple founded in 628 AD. Arrive early (8:00–9:00 AM) to beat the crowds. Walk through the iconic Thunder Gate (Kaminarimon), stroll the Nakamise shopping arcade for souvenirs and traditional snacks like ningyo-yaki and senbei.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Senso-ji, take the subway to Ueno Park – one of Tokyo's top cherry blossom spots in mid-April. Enjoy a relaxed hanami (flower viewing) picnic under the blossoming trees. Visit the Ueno Zoo for a family-friendly activity, or explore the Tokyo National Museum for a dose of Japanese history and culture.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Akihabara district for a lively evening of exploring electronics shops, anime culture, and quirky themed cafes. Families can enjoy the multi-floor arcades and claw machine games. Wind down with a stroll through the illuminated streets.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a traditional Japanese morning set (tamago gohan, miso soup, grilled fish) at a local kissaten (coffee shop) near the hotel – ¥600–¥1,200
meals.lunch: Asakusa Imahan or a nearby tempura restaurant in Asakusa for a mid-range set lunch (¥1,500–¥2,500 per person)
meals.dinner: Akihabara ramen or a family-friendly izakaya near Ueno – try Fuunji-style tsukemen or a hearty tonkotsu ramen (¥1,000–¥2,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Cherry blossoms in mid-April may be in late bloom or petals falling (hanafubuki) – still beautiful! Wear comfortable walking shoes. Senso-ji is free to enter. Ueno Zoo tickets are approximately ¥600 for adults, ¥200 for children.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Shinkansen (bullet train) from Tokyo to Kyoto (approximately 2 hours 15 minutes on the Nozomi). Arrive in Kyoto and check in or drop luggage at a day-storage locker at Kyoto Station. Head directly to Maruyama Park for the iconic Cherry Blossom Viewing experience – witness the legendary weeping cherry tree (shidarezakura) in full splendor and enjoy a relaxed hanami among locals.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Gion District adjacent to Maruyama Park – Kyoto's famous geisha quarter. Walk along Hanamikoji Street, admire traditional machiya townhouses, and if lucky, spot a maiko or geiko in the late afternoon. Visit Yasaka Shrine within the park complex.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Shirakawa Canal in Gion as lanterns and cherry blossoms create a magical atmosphere after dark. Enjoy a traditional Kyoto kaiseki-inspired dinner in the neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at Tokyo Station's underground food hall (Gransta) before boarding the Shinkansen – try an ekiben (station bento box, ¥1,000–¥1,500)
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch in Maruyama Park – pick up bento boxes, onigiri, and taiyaki from stalls around the park (¥800–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Gion Kappa or a mid-range kaiseki-style restaurant in Gion for Kyoto cuisine – tofu dishes, yudofu, and seasonal vegetables (¥3,000–¥5,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book Shinkansen tickets in advance (JR Pass recommended for this trip). Maruyama Park is free to enter and is most magical in the evening when the weeping cherry tree is illuminated. Gion is a walking-friendly neighborhood – no transportation needed between afternoon and evening activities.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to Fushimi Inari Taisha – the famous shrine with thousands of vermillion torii gates winding up the mountain. Arrive by 7:00–8:00 AM for a peaceful, crowd-free experience. Hike as far as the family is comfortable (the full hike takes 2–3 hours; even 30–45 minutes up the trail is rewarding).
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel to the Arashiyama district. Walk through the ethereal Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and cross the iconic Togetsukyo Bridge over the Oi River. Visit Tenryu-ji Temple and its stunning garden (a UNESCO World Heritage Site). Families can enjoy a rickshaw ride through the bamboo grove area.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Kyoto. Visit Nishiki Market – Kyoto's 'Kitchen' – for evening browsing and tasting local street food like grilled skewers, pickled vegetables, and tamagoyaki. Relax at the hotel or explore Kyoto Station's Isetan department store basement food hall.

meals.breakfast: Early convenience store breakfast near Fushimi Inari or hotel breakfast before departure (¥500–¥1,000)
meals.lunch: Arashiyama tofu cuisine – try Shigetsu restaurant inside Tenryu-ji for a vegetarian Buddhist shojin ryori set lunch (¥3,000–¥4,000) or a casual soba noodle shop nearby (¥1,000–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Nishiki Market street food crawl followed by a sit-down dinner at a local izakaya near Kyoto Station (¥2,000–¥3,500 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Fushimi Inari is free and open 24/7. Tenryu-ji garden admission is ¥500 (garden only) or ¥800 (including temple interior). The Bamboo Grove is free to walk through. Arashiyama can be reached from central Kyoto by the JR Sagano Line or Randen tram.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Nijo Castle – a UNESCO World Heritage Site and former shogun residence famous for its 'nightingale floors' that chirp when walked upon, a historical anti-assassination feature. Admire the Ninomaru Palace interiors and the beautiful castle gardens with late cherry blossoms.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Kinkaku-ji (the Golden Pavilion) – one of Japan's most iconic landmarks, a Zen Buddhist temple covered in gold leaf reflecting on a tranquil pond. Afterward, explore the nearby Ryoan-ji Temple with its famous rock garden, a masterpiece of Zen minimalism.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Philosopher's Path (Tetsugaku-no-Michi) for a gentle evening stroll along the canal lined with cherry trees – a romantic and serene end to a culture-rich day. End with dinner in the Nanzen-ji area.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a Kyoto-style morning set at a local cafe (¥700–¥1,200)
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at a noodle shop near Kinkaku-ji – kitsune udon or soba (¥900–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Nanzen-ji area restaurant for yudofu (hot tofu) dinner, a Kyoto specialty – Junsei or Okutan restaurants (¥3,000–¥4,500 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Nijo Castle admission is ¥1,030 for adults. Kinkaku-ji admission is ¥500. Ryoan-ji admission is ¥600. The Philosopher's Path is free and approximately 2 km long – perfect for families with children. Book popular restaurants in advance on weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nara – easily accessible from Kyoto by train (45 minutes on the Kintetsu Limited Express). Visit Todai-ji Temple, home to Japan's largest bronze Buddha statue. Walk through Nara Park where hundreds of freely roaming sacred deer will bow for shika senbei (deer crackers) – an unforgettable family activity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kasuga Taisha Shrine – a UNESCO World Heritage Site famous for its hundreds of bronze and stone lanterns. Walk the forested paths and enjoy the peaceful atmosphere. Visit Naramachi, the preserved merchant district, for traditional crafts and sweets.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kyoto by early evening. Enjoy a relaxed evening in Kyoto – perhaps a sento (public bath) experience for the family or evening shopping at Teramachi and Shinkyogoku covered shopping arcades.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or onigiri from a convenience store before the train (¥500–¥1,000)
meals.lunch: Nara kakinoha-zushi (persimmon leaf sushi) at a local restaurant in Naramachi or a bento from a Nara station shop (¥1,200–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: Teramachi area izakaya or a family-friendly Japanese restaurant in central Kyoto (¥2,000–¥3,500 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Deer crackers (shika senbei) cost approximately ¥200 per bundle – children will love feeding the deer! Todai-ji admission is ¥600 for adults. Kasuga Taisha is free to enter (inner sanctum has a fee). The Kintetsu Limited Express requires a small surcharge on top of the regular fare.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Shinkansen from Kyoto to Hiroshima (approximately 1 hour). Head directly to the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum & Park – a deeply moving and historically essential experience. Tour the museum thoughtfully, view the A-Bomb Dome (Genbaku Dome), and walk through the Peace Memorial Park. A profoundly important visit for families with older children.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short ferry from Hiroshima to Miyajima Island (Itsukushima) – a UNESCO World Heritage Site. See the famous floating torii gate of Itsukushima Shrine at high or low tide (both offer stunning views). Walk the island, encounter friendly deer, and explore the shrine complex.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hiroshima city for dinner. Explore Hiroshima's famous local specialties. Return to Kyoto by Shinkansen in the late evening, or if budget allows, consider staying one night in Hiroshima.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at Kyoto Station before boarding – station bakery or onigiri (¥600–¥1,000)
meals.lunch: Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki (savory pancake with noodles) at Okonomimura – a multi-floor building filled with okonomiyaki stalls, a must-try local experience (¥1,000–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Hiroshima oyster restaurant – the city is famous for its plump, fresh oysters grilled or served raw (¥2,500–¥4,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Peace Memorial Museum is appropriate for children aged 10+ but may be emotionally intense – prepare children beforehand. Museum admission is ¥200 for adults, free for children. The ferry to Miyajima costs approximately ¥380 each way (covered by JR Pass). Check tide times for the floating torii gate at miyajima.or.jp.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Tokyo by Shinkansen (if not already back). Upon arrival, head to the Tsukiji Outer Market for a late morning food tour – explore the bustling stalls of fresh seafood, tamagoyaki, and Japanese street food. Sample fresh tuna sashimi, uni, and grilled scallops from various vendors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the teamLab Borderless or teamLab Planets digital art museum (book tickets in advance) for a family-friendly, immersive, and culturally unique experience. Alternatively, explore the Hamarikyu Gardens – a beautiful traditional Japanese garden with a teahouse, located near Tsukiji.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shibuya for the iconic Shibuya Scramble Crossing experience. View it from the Starbucks or Mag's Park observation deck. Explore Shibuya's vibrant shopping streets and enjoy dinner in the area.

meals.breakfast: Light hotel breakfast or grab-and-go from a convenience store (¥500–¥800)
meals.lunch: Tsukiji Outer Market food crawl – budget ¥2,000–¥3,500 per person for a satisfying spread of sushi, sashimi, tamagoyaki, and fresh seafood
meals.dinner: Shibuya restaurant – try a mid-range shabu-shabu or sukiyaki restaurant for a fun, interactive family dining experience (¥3,000–¥5,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market is busiest in the morning – arrive by 9:00–10:00 AM for the best selection. teamLab tickets must be booked online in advance and sell out weeks ahead. Hamarikyu Gardens admission is ¥300 for adults. The Shibuya Scramble is best experienced at dusk or night when the neon lights are vivid.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden – one of Tokyo's largest and most beautiful parks, with a blend of Japanese, French, and English garden styles. In mid-to-late April, late-blooming cherry varieties (like Ichiyo and Kanzan) may still be in bloom. A peaceful morning stroll perfect for families.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Edo-Tokyo Museum (or Tokyo City View at Mori Tower in Roppongi) for a deep dive into Tokyo's history from the Edo period to the modern era. Interactive exhibits make it engaging for children. Alternatively, explore the teamLab experience if not visited yesterday.
day_by_day.evening: Evening visit to Tokyo Tower or Tokyo Skytree for panoramic night views of the city. The illuminated city skyline is breathtaking. Enjoy dinner in the surrounding area – Asakusa (near Skytree) or Shiba (near Tokyo Tower) both have excellent dining options.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a morning set at a local Doutor or Komeda's Coffee – a popular Japanese chain with hearty morning menus (¥500–¥900)
meals.lunch: Shinjuku area lunch – try a mid-range sushi conveyor belt restaurant (kaiten-zushi) like Sushiro or Kurasushi (¥1,500–¥2,500 per person)
meals.dinner: Asakusa or Shiba area – yakitori restaurant or a family-friendly tempura donburi restaurant (¥2,000–¥3,500 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Shinjuku Gyoen admission is ¥500 for adults, ¥250 for children. Note that alcohol is not permitted inside the garden. Tokyo Skytree observation deck tickets range from ¥2,100–¥3,100 for adults. Book online to avoid queues. The Edo-Tokyo Museum may be partially under renovation – check current status before visiting.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Japan – take a leisurely stroll through Yanaka, one of Tokyo's best-preserved old-town neighborhoods that survived WWII. Explore the Yanaka Ginza shopping street for traditional crafts, local snacks, and a glimpse of old Shitamachi (downtown) Tokyo life. Visit the Yanaka Cemetery, famous for its cherry blossoms.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Harajuku for a final dose of Japanese pop culture – visit Takeshita Street for quirky fashion and crepes, then walk down Omotesando Avenue for upscale boutiques and beautiful zelkova tree-lined streets. Pick up last-minute gifts and souvenirs. Visit Don Quijote or a department store basement food hall (depachika) for omiyage (souvenir sweets and snacks).
day_by_day.evening: Final farewell dinner in Tokyo – celebrate the journey with a special meal. Head to the airport for departure (check flight time and allow 3 hours for international check-in). Reflect on an incredible 10 days in Japan.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast – enjoy a full meal before checking out (included or ¥1,000–¥1,500)
meals.lunch: Harajuku crepe from Marion Crepes or Angel's Heart (¥500–¥800) followed by a casual ramen lunch at a Harajuku or Omotesando ramen shop (¥900–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Splurge farewell dinner – a teppanyaki or high-quality sushi restaurant in Ginza or Shinjuku (¥5,000–¥8,000 per person) OR a comforting bowl of ramen at a famous shop like Ichiran for a memorable final meal (¥1,200–¥1,500)

day_by_day.notes: Check out of the hotel and store luggage at the hotel or a coin locker at a nearby train station for the final day of exploring. Allow ample time to reach the airport – Narita is 60–90 minutes from central Tokyo; Haneda is 30–45 minutes. Purchase any remaining omiyage at the airport duty-free shops. Unused Suica card balance can be refunded at station service centers.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Japan Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park
experiences.description: Experience hanami (flower viewing) under the iconic weeping cherry tree in Kyoto's most famous park. Join locals for picnics beneath thousands of blooming sakura trees, with food stalls offering traditional snacks like sakura mochi and taiyaki. The park is especially magical at night when lanterns illuminate the blossoms.

experiences.name: Senso-ji Temple & Nakamise Shopping Street
experiences.description: Visit Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple, founded in 628 AD. Walk through the Thunder Gate (Kaminarimon) and explore the vibrant Nakamise shopping street lined with traditional craft shops and street food vendors. Families can try fortune-telling omikuji slips and dress in rented kimono for memorable photos.

experiences.name: Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum & Park
experiences.description: A deeply moving and historically essential experience for families. Tour the Peace Memorial Museum to understand the events of 1945 through personal artifacts and testimonies, then walk through the Peace Memorial Park to see the Atomic Bomb Dome. Children can fold origami cranes at the Children's Peace Monument, connecting with Sadako's powerful story.
experiences.location: Peace Memorial Park, Naka Ward, Hiroshima

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into Japan's legendary food culture with a self-guided or guided tour of the Tsukiji Outer Market. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), grilled scallops, matcha ice cream, and wagyu beef skewers. This is an ideal family activity that introduces everyone to authentic Japanese flavors in a lively, accessible market setting.
experiences.location: Tsukiji Outer Market, Chuo City, Tokyo

experiences.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove & Togetsukyo Bridge
experiences.description: Wander through the ethereal bamboo forest of Arashiyama, one of Japan's most iconic natural and cultural landscapes. Extend the experience with a rickshaw ride through the historic district, visit the Tenryu-ji Zen garden (a UNESCO World Heritage Site), and stroll across the Togetsukyo Bridge with stunning mountain and cherry blossom backdrops in spring. Perfect for all ages.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight UA arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at the airport at 22:30. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange private luxury transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your beachfront suite. A welcome amenity and late-night turndown service awaits.

meals.breakfast: On board or at airport
meals.lunch: On board or at airport
meals.dinner: Late-night in-room dining at Aegean Bliss Resort — request a curated Japanese welcome platter with sake, seasonal sashimi, and miso soup

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a private airport transfer through the resort concierge. Request early check-in amenities and a Japanese welcome gift (yukata, matcha, wagashi sweets). Keep Day 1 light — rest is essential for the days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely resort morning — enjoy a premium Japanese breakfast at the resort's oceanfront restaurant featuring grilled fish, tamago, miso soup, pickles, and steamed rice. Take a slow stroll along the beachfront to acclimate and recover from jet lag. Visit the resort spa for a rejuvenating onsen bath or shiatsu massage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local surroundings near the resort. Visit a nearby cultural landmark, local shrine, or garden. Engage with the resort concierge to finalize all upcoming excursion bookings, private guide arrangements, and restaurant reservations for the full trip.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a refined kaiseki dinner at the resort's signature restaurant — a multi-course Japanese haute cuisine experience featuring seasonal ingredients, local seafood, and expertly paired sake or Japanese whisky.

meals.breakfast: Japanese breakfast set at the resort's oceanfront restaurant
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort's poolside café — try chirashi don (scattered sushi bowl) and cold matcha
meals.dinner: Kaiseki dinner at the resort's signature dining room — 8-10 course seasonal tasting menu

day_by_day.notes: Use this day as a gentle orientation day. Confirm all bookings for Kyoto and Tokyo excursions. Request the resort concierge to arrange Shinkansen (bullet train) tickets for upcoming travel days.

day_by_day.morning: Depart by private luxury transfer to the nearest Shinkansen station. Board a reserved Green Car (first-class) bullet train to Kyoto. Arrive in Kyoto mid-morning and check in or store luggage at a luxury Kyoto property (arrange day-use room or luggage storage). Head directly to Maruyama Park for the Cherry Blossom Viewing (Hanami) experience — witness the iconic weeping cherry tree in full bloom, stroll the park grounds, and enjoy the serene springtime atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Kyoto cultural immersion with a visit to Arashiyama — wander through the ethereal Bamboo Grove, cross the historic Togetsukyo Bridge over the Oi River, and explore the charming riverside district. Hire a private rickshaw (jinrikisha) for a premium tour of the Arashiyama area.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Kyoto for a private tea ceremony experience at an exclusive machiya (traditional townhouse) tea room. Enjoy a premium Kyoto kaiseki dinner at a renowned Gion restaurant overlooking a traditional garden.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium tofu cuisine restaurant in Arashiyama — try yudofu (hot tofu) and seasonal vegetable dishes
meals.dinner: Kaiseki dinner at a top-rated Gion restaurant such as Kichisen or Mizai — reserve well in advance

day_by_day.notes: April is peak cherry blossom season — Maruyama Park will be spectacular but crowded. Arrive early (before 9 AM) for the best experience. Book the Gion kaiseki dinner months in advance as top Kyoto restaurants fill quickly during sakura season.

day_by_day.morning: Full day in Kyoto. Begin with an early morning private guided tour of Fushimi Inari Shrine — hike the iconic vermillion torii gate trail at dawn before the crowds arrive. Explore the forested mountain paths and enjoy panoramic views over Kyoto. This is a culturally rich and visually stunning family experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Nishiki Market ('Kyoto's Kitchen') for a premium food tasting walk — sample wagyu skewers, tamagoyaki, pickled vegetables, matcha sweets, and fresh dango. Afterward, explore the historic Gion district on foot — spot geisha (maiko) in traditional dress along Hanamikoji Street. Visit Kennin-ji Temple, Kyoto's oldest Zen temple.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private Maiko (apprentice geisha) dinner performance — an exclusive cultural experience where a Maiko performs traditional dances, plays the shamisen, and engages guests in refined conversation over an exquisite multi-course dinner. Book through a specialist cultural experience company.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at a Kyoto café — try a traditional Japanese morning set with coffee
meals.lunch: Premium wagyu beef lunch at a top Kyoto yakiniku restaurant in the Kawaramachi area
meals.dinner: Private Maiko dinner experience — a once-in-a-lifetime cultural and culinary event

day_by_day.notes: The Maiko dinner experience must be booked weeks or months in advance through a reputable cultural agency. Children are generally welcome but should be briefed on etiquette. Fushimi Inari at dawn is magical — depart by 6:00 AM for the best experience.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nara from Kyoto (45 minutes by limited express train). Visit Todai-ji Temple, home to Japan's largest bronze Buddha statue, and stroll through Nara Park where over 1,200 semi-wild deer roam freely — a beloved family activity. Purchase deer crackers (shika senbei) to feed the deer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kasuga Taisha Grand Shrine, one of Japan's most important Shinto shrines, lined with hundreds of stone and bronze lanterns. Walk through the ancient Naramachi district — a preserved merchant quarter with traditional machiya townhouses now converted into artisan shops and cafés. Browse for premium lacquerware and Nara crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kyoto by early evening. Enjoy a relaxing evening stroll along the Philosopher's Path (Tetsugaku-no-michi) — a canal-side walkway lined with cherry trees still in late bloom. Dinner in the Higashiyama district.

meals.breakfast: Japanese breakfast at the Kyoto hotel or a local kissaten (coffee shop)
meals.lunch: Lunch in Nara at a premium restaurant near Todai-ji — try kakinoha-zushi (persimmon leaf sushi), a Nara specialty
meals.dinner: Dinner at a refined Higashiyama restaurant — try kaiseki or premium shabu-shabu with Kyoto vegetables

day_by_day.notes: Nara is extremely family-friendly. Children love interacting with the deer. Remind children not to tease or hold food too long as deer can nip. The Philosopher's Path cherry blossoms may be in late bloom by April 19 — still beautiful with falling petals (hanafubuki).

day_by_day.morning: Depart Kyoto by Shinkansen (Green Car) to Hiroshima — approximately 1 hour 15 minutes. Arrive and head directly to the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Park. Take a deeply moving and historically essential guided tour of the museum, which chronicles the 1945 atomic bombing. Walk through the Peace Memorial Park, view the Atomic Bomb Dome (Genbaku Dome), and ring the Peace Bell.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short ferry ride to Miyajima Island — one of Japan's most scenic and sacred locations. Visit Itsukushima Shrine and its iconic floating torii gate. Hike or take the ropeway to the top of Mt. Misen for panoramic views. Explore the island's friendly deer and charming shopping streets. Try Miyajima's famous momiji manju (maple leaf cakes).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hiroshima city by ferry and train. Enjoy a premium Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki dinner — the local savory pancake layered with noodles, cabbage, and your choice of toppings, prepared at a high-end teppan counter.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast on the Shinkansen or at Hiroshima Station
meals.lunch: Lunch on Miyajima Island — try fresh grilled oysters (Hiroshima is Japan's top oyster region) at a waterfront restaurant
meals.dinner: Premium Hiroshima okonomiyaki at Hassho or a top-rated teppanyaki restaurant in the city center

day_by_day.notes: The Peace Memorial Museum is deeply emotional and sobering — prepare children with age-appropriate context beforehand. The museum is historically invaluable and recommended for families. Miyajima is magical at sunset — try to time your visit accordingly. Book the Hiroshima-to-Tokyo Shinkansen for tomorrow morning.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Hiroshima by Shinkansen (Nozomi, Green Car) to Tokyo — approximately 4 hours. Arrive in Tokyo and transfer by private car to your Tokyo luxury hotel (e.g., The Peninsula Tokyo, Aman Tokyo, or Park Hyatt Tokyo). Check in and freshen up. Head to the Tsukiji Outer Market for a premium guided food tour — sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, sea urchin, wagyu beef skewers, and seasonal Japanese street food.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Senso-ji Temple in Asakusa — Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple founded in 628 AD. Walk through the Kaminarimon (Thunder Gate) and along the Nakamise Shopping Street, browsing for premium Japanese souvenirs, traditional crafts, fans, and sweets. Explore the historic Asakusa district on foot or by private rickshaw.
day_by_day.evening: Ascend Tokyo Skytree (reserve premium floor access) for breathtaking panoramic views of Tokyo at dusk and into the evening. Enjoy dinner at a world-class Tokyo restaurant — try Sukiyabashi Jiro (if reservations are possible) or another Michelin-starred sushi or teppanyaki establishment.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast on the Shinkansen or at Hiroshima hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Premium sushi and market tastings at Tsukiji Outer Market — curated guided food tour
meals.dinner: Michelin-starred dinner in Tokyo — omakase sushi, premium teppanyaki, or French-Japanese fusion

day_by_day.notes: Tokyo is a major shift in pace from Kyoto — embrace the energy. Tsukiji Outer Market (the outer market remains open; the inner wholesale market moved to Toyosu) is still a world-class food destination. Book Michelin-starred restaurants months in advance. Tokyo Skytree tickets can be pre-purchased online.

day_by_day.morning: Full day in Tokyo. Begin with a morning visit to the Imperial Palace East Gardens — a serene and historically significant green space in the heart of Tokyo, free to the public. Walk across the iconic Nijubashi Bridge and enjoy the cherry blossom aftermath (late petals and fresh green leaves). Continue to the Meiji Jingu Shrine in Harajuku — a magnificent forested Shinto shrine dedicated to Emperor Meiji, offering a tranquil cultural contrast to the bustling city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Harajuku and Omotesando — Tokyo's most fashionable district. Browse luxury Japanese and international boutiques along Omotesando Hills (Japan's answer to the Champs-Élysées). Visit a premium matcha café for an afternoon break. Head to Shibuya to witness the world-famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing — best viewed from the Scramble Square observation deck or a café above street level.
day_by_day.evening: Evening in Shinjuku — explore the vibrant Golden Gai district for a cultural drink at a tiny atmospheric bar. Enjoy a premium Japanese whisky tasting experience at a top-rated whisky bar. Dinner at a high-end Shinjuku restaurant — try premium kaiseki, omakase, or a world-class ramen experience elevated to fine dining.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Tokyo hotel — Japanese or Western set at the hotel's restaurant
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium restaurant in Omotesando — try a refined Japanese lunch course or artisanal wagyu burger
meals.dinner: Fine dining dinner in Shinjuku — try Nakamura Tokichi's seasonal menu or a renowned teppanyaki counter

day_by_day.notes: Omotesando is ideal for premium shopping — look for Japanese designer brands, ceramics, and unique artisan goods as souvenirs. The Meiji Shrine forest walk is a beautiful, calming family experience. Book Shibuya Sky or Scramble Square observation deck tickets online in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip or half-day excursion to Nikko (2 hours from Tokyo by limited express train) — a UNESCO World Heritage Site featuring the extraordinarily ornate Toshogu Shrine, dedicated to Tokugawa Ieyasu. Marvel at the intricate wood carvings, gilded architecture, and forested mountain setting. Visit the famous Yomeimon Gate (Gate of Sunlight) and the sacred Shinkyo Bridge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Tokyo by early afternoon. Spend the afternoon at teamLab Planets or teamLab Borderless (whichever is currently open) — an immersive and awe-inspiring digital art museum that is a spectacular family experience blending technology, art, and nature. Book premium time-slot tickets well in advance.
day_by_day.evening: Final full evening in Tokyo — enjoy a celebratory luxury dinner at one of Tokyo's finest rooftop or view restaurants. Consider Signatures at the Hotel de Crillon-style venues or the New York Bar at the Park Hyatt Tokyo (famous from Lost in Translation). Enjoy premium cocktails and live jazz with sweeping city views.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departing for Nikko
meals.lunch: Lunch in Nikko — try yuba (tofu skin) cuisine, a Nikko specialty, at a traditional restaurant near the shrine complex
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at a premium Tokyo rooftop restaurant or the New York Bar at Park Hyatt Tokyo

day_by_day.notes: Nikko is a stunning historical and natural destination — highly recommended for history and culture enthusiasts. teamLab tickets must be booked online well in advance as they sell out quickly. The New York Bar at Park Hyatt requires smart casual dress and a reservation.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo. Enjoy a leisurely premium hotel breakfast. Take a final stroll through a nearby park or garden — Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden is perfect for a last cherry blossom (or post-bloom green garden) experience. Do any last-minute luxury shopping at Isetan Department Store in Shinjuku for premium Japanese food gifts, cosmetics, and crafts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrange private luxury transfer to the airport (Narita or Haneda). Allow ample time for check-in, duty-free shopping, and relaxing in the premium airport lounge. Depart Japan with extraordinary memories.
day_by_day.evening: In transit — enjoy the airline's premium cabin service.

meals.breakfast: Final premium Japanese breakfast at the Tokyo hotel — savor every bite
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport or Isetan food hall — pick up premium Japanese bento, onigiri, or a final bowl of ramen
meals.dinner: On board in business or first class

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before departure for airport check-in, immigration, and security — especially at Narita. Haneda is closer to central Tokyo (45 min vs. 90 min). Purchase duty-free Japanese whisky, sake, wagashi, and cosmetics at the airport. Confirm return transfer with the resort concierge the night before.
